A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical bracketing work. Their text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original parsing experiments on nine UD treebanks, development/test accuracy and coverage results, and inference-speed measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds Penn Treebank results, hexatagging comparisons, and measured training/inference emissions.

M1.justification: The rope-cover construction, encodings, Algorithms 1–2, neural architecture, and training loss are unchanged. The new well-formedness paragraph documents implementation behavior without establishing a change to the method.

E1.justification: V2 adds the English Penn Treebank to training/evaluation coverage (Tables 2–4). All nine UD 2.14 treebanks remain, with no additional language or parsing task.

E2.justification: Hexatagging, previously cited but not evaluated, becomes a systematic comparator as pseudo-projective H+ across the retained treebanks and English speed comparison. This adds an important competing bounded-label approach while retaining the 4-bit, 7-bit, and biaffine baselines.

E3.justification: The new hexatagging evaluations use pseudo-projective preprocessing and the authors' implementation for homogeneous comparison. V2 also introduces per-epoch CO2 measurement. The retained experiments keep their stated metrics, encoder sizes, training budget, learning rate, batch size, and stopping rule.

E4.justification: The existing accuracy–speed analysis gains H+ measurements, extending the comparison between label compactness and runtime. V2 also adds a carbon-footprint analysis. The new step-by-step encoding figure is explanatory; no new ablation or robustness suite appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. V2's cross-treebank averages summarize results rather than introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds PTB and H+ results, averages, and emissions measurements, and revises numerous appendix coverage values. For example, Ancient Greek B7 empirical test LAS changes from 85.43 in v1 Table 5 to 99.19 in v2 Table 6. Most retained trained-model scores are unchanged. Finnish O+P LCM changes from 44.37 to 44.74 in Table 3, although v2 Table 7 still reports 44.37.

T1.justification: V2 adds runtime arguments for Algorithm 1, including O(n) for trees, and an O(|A| i_max^2) bound for Algorithm 2 in Appendix A.1. It also changes the inner arc-cover inequality from <= to <. Theorems 1–3, Corollary 1, and their proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and concluding contributions retain the same claims: optimal hierarchical bracketing, 12 versus 16 projective labels, arbitrary non-projective support, and competitive accuracy. The introduction clarifies the existing pseudo-projectivity claim without changing its scope.

C2.justification: V2 discusses malformed label sequences and explains hexatagging's runtime disadvantage through intermediate constituency-tree conversion. It adds interpretations of the expanded comparisons and emissions measurements. The existing compactness–redundancy explanation and fine-tuning/resource limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 discloses unmatched-bracket handling, cycle/reentrancy checks, and attachment of parentless nodes to the root. It states that the released code includes the authors' hexatagging implementation and notes possible hyperparameter differences from the original implementation. Existing model settings, hardware disclosure, and code address remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds Marcus et al. (1993) for Penn Treebank and expands the comparison with hexatagging's accuracy and computational requirements. The broader positioning relative to rope-cover theory and previous bracketing encodings is retained.

P1.justification: Changes include localized wording and directional corrections, expanded decoding explanations, and a new Ethical considerations section. The speed discussion moves from Appendix A.3 into Section 5, and detailed results become Appendix A.3. The main narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: V2 adds the step-by-step Figure 4 and retains the former Figure 4 as Figure 6. Figure 5 moves into the main text and gains H+ points. Tables gain hexatagging entries, PTB results, and averages, while the established diagram styles and two-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: Evaluating the previously unevaluated hexatagging competitor and adding PTB strengthen the empirical context. Decoding heuristics, runtime arguments, and the worked example improve documentation. These gains are limited by new reporting inconsistencies: Russian H+ LAS is 88.71 in Table 3 but 87.61 in Table 10, and PTB H+ LAS is 94.80 in Table 3 but printed as 04.80 in Table 4.
